recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-5679 unless a later FHIR-I decision changes _revinclude syntax or CapabilityStatement advertisement semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-5679 was Published/Persuasive for DSTU1 and asked to add reverse include so a search could retrieve resources, such as Provenance, that point back to the matched resource. The recorded FHIR Core decision specified search-parameter syntax rather than paths, examples for include and reverse include, and repeated parameters rather than comma-separated values.
initial_application: The Jira application note cites SVN revision 4580. The corresponding git-svn commit 13da0d4b9ad91765695173ebcd8b31387120f812 changed source/search.html for '#5679 and #3356: _revinclude and changes to _include', replacing path-based include wording with search-parameter-based _include/_revinclude syntax and adding the Provenance:target reverse-include example.
additional_context: Current source/search.html remains the active top-level Search source page and preserves the approved behavior: _revinclude follows reverse links using search parameters, shares the resource/search-parameter/targetType syntax with _include, is repeated for multiple criteria, and includes the Provenance:target example. CapabilityStatement.rest.resource.searchRevInclude is present for advertising supported reverse includes. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no FHIR-5679-specific record that changes this conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current specification already implements the requested reverse include behavior and uses the search-parameter syntax approved by FHIR-I.

related_jiras.note: The original SVN/git application commit also handled FHIR-3356 by clarifying _include recursion behavior on the same Search page; that separate issue was not independently reconciled here.
